title: Episode 27: The Dungeon Dive at Disneyland
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i4tThjQW98w

A short episode recorded the week Daniel (@dungeondive) left for Disneyland with his extended family, published to land while he was inside the park. He starts by drawing a line: he dislikes Disney the corporation, the Marvel-isation of genre cinema and the flood of Star Wars product, but he has a deep soft spot for vintage Disney. Carl Barks and Don Rosa duck comics, the Goofy sports shorts, Humphrey the Bear, and Disney Channel afternoons at his grandmother's house with Eggo waffles are named as cherished memories. The park itself has never lost its magic for him, even approaching fifty, and he still remembers the day-after-Christmas sadness of leaving it as a child.

Two losses get mourned: the Country Bear Jamboree, Big Al in particular, and the Starcade arcade under Space Mountain with its full hydraulic *After Burner* cabinet. Then a top five. Main Street shopping for the magic shop and the Disneyland history books. The Indiana Jones queue, praised as an immersive set in its own right. The Haunted Mansion, which terrified him as a boy. Pirates of the Caribbean, the ride he would live in if he could, and his prime example of the artificial environments he loves. At number one, the Enchanted Tiki Room, the capstone of every childhood visit.

----

Daniel ranks a queue line among his top five attractions. What piece of theme-park or game presentation do you think outshines the main event?
